B. WHY THE SPEC ENGINE EXISTS, WHAT IT IS FOR, ITS SCOPE AND ITS BOUNDARIES (the "why" behind every rule below)

B1. THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES
The front-end engine is an LLM (with a component library and many MCP tools attached) that writes the Expo / React Native / TypeScript app for iOS and Android. If it were handed only the approved Brief it would have to INVENT the product's logic (who the users are, what data exists, what the rules are, what every screen must show and do, what the API looks like, how errors, permissions and offline behave) AND decide how everything looks, in one pass, inside a finite context window. The result would be slow, inconsistent between screens, full of guesses and visually generic. Compass produces the approved Brief (what the user wants, with verified quotes). Research produces facts (market, regulation, payment and other providers, what peer apps do). Neither is something a developer can build from. SPEC translates them into ONE complete, checkable description of WHAT THE APP IS AND DOES, cut into layers that fit the front end's context window, so the front end can spend its effort on how each screen LOOKS AND FEELS. Spec is the outermost, most important engine of the context part: whatever it hands over is all the front end will ever know about the product.

B2. THE ONE LINE THAT DECIDES EVERY FIELD
MEANING is Spec's: who, what, data, rules, flows, states, words, API contract, behaviour. EXPRESSION is the front end's: layout, components, motion, imagery, icons, visual hierarchy. Spec may say how things USUALLY are (the USUALLY voice, from evidence) and how they COULD be better (the COULD voice, ideas with a basis); it gives tokens and a design direction as a starting system the front end may extend; it never binds. Whatever Spec does not say, the front end decides ("the rule of silence"). Over-specified input makes the front end build the same template for every app; under-specified input makes it guess. The owner wants a visually advanced, animated 2026 mobile app, never a generic web app.

B3. WHO CONSUMES SPEC'S OUTPUT, AND HOW
- The FRONT-END ENGINE: reads the Spec Pack as files (or through a thin Spec Server): small packs whole where its window allows, medium packs by module and screen, big packs only through TASK CARDS (28k tokens of reads each). It may build screens in parallel, one by one or all at once, so the pack must be STATIC, SELF-CONTAINED and ORDER-INDEPENDENT. It writes its own artifacts (component-map.json, a design-language record, deviations.json, raise_decision files); Spec never writes those.
- The OWNER: reads the G1.5 view (structure, phase split, consent) and the G2 view (summary, flows, content maps, confirm list, what differs from the Brief, check report) and approves; G2 binds the content hash. Later G3 is the preview built from the pack.
- The BACKEND ENGINE: builds from Contract v0 (OpenAPI, schemas, errors, auth matrix, events, fixtures).
- The QA ENGINE: uses acceptance scenarios, the stable region and action keys (they become testIDs) and the mock profiles.
- The CHANGE CONTROLLER (after G2): files change sets; Spec is the single writer that applies them by incremental regeneration.
- VERIFY (deep apps): checks Spec's output and proposes patches; Spec applies them.

B4. SCOPE
IN SCOPE: apps, roles and the access matrix; modules; entities, fields and lifecycles; rules and derived fields; the screen inventory (DERIVED, never a fixed count); a card per screen (information regions with importance levels, actions as intents with typed effects and guards, states, copy keys, inputs with semantic types, acceptance scenarios, analytics, accessibility, mock references, stories, COULD ideas in their own file); navigation (entries, exits, typed route parameters, guards); Contract v0 for the screens' API; integrations as provider-neutral flows (interrupted-flow and pending-timeout rules); global behaviour (session, offline and sync, error taxonomy and recovery, permissions, notifications, i18n and right-to-left, analytics with consent, client state slices, media fallbacks); design direction and tokens; copy per locale; personas, user stories and journeys with emotion; the mock data model; the build plan (task cards, waves, ownership, pilot picks); phases and the scope ledger; the G1.5 and G2 data; the check reports; incremental regeneration after changes.
OUT OF SCOPE (never do these): layout, grid, spacing choices, component or widget names, positions, pixels, colours outside tokens, animation choices, imagery, icon choice, per-screen visual hints; choosing a component library or a package (the Stack Kit is fixed data); writing app code or pseudo-code; web search (Research does that); interviewing the user (Compass); implementing the backend; running QA; hosting or store submission; pricing; plugging Spec into the main flow (a later adapter, designed here, not built now).

B5. NEIGHBOURS AND THEIR CONTRACTS
- COMPASS gives the approved Brief in formats 1, 2 or trimmed (read through ONE shared reader, packages/compass-intake, extracted from Research's intake/formats.py). Compass's structure (screens, phases, flows) is a PROPOSAL Spec refines. Verified quotes make a feature's existence Locked; Compass's `priority` is unreliable (the real Thorough export marks 26 of 30 features `nice`); roles and apps can be duplicated or junk; integrations are often thin; entities average 3 to 4 fields. The nine real and test exports in docs/compass/research-inputs/ are the adapter test corpus.
- RESEARCH gives research.v5 (facts with evidence levels, provider dossiers, platform constraints, a thin compliance register, a ranked confirm list) read through pack(need_card) by Brief id (docs/research-agent/spec-contract.md). Partial, skipped or failed Research is a thin lane, never a crash. Rules R21 to R28 decide what may be a Default.
- The FRONT END owns every decision about form. VERIFY only checks. The CHANGE CONTROLLER does steps 1 to 6 of the change pipeline (doc 05) and Spec does step 7.

B6. SIZES AND SCALE
The user's tier (Quick, Standard, Thorough) and the Brief's size band set a detail profile FLOOR: compact, standard, deep; content can only raise it (two or more apps, sensitive data, three or more integrations, three or more locales or a right-to-left script, offline-first use, four or more apps or eight or more modules). Typical: compact = one app, 10 to 20 screens; standard = 1 to 4 apps, about 25 to 45 screens in total; deep = a PROGRAM of several apps, 50 to 60 screens per app at the front end's per-run capacity (scope_cap_per_app_phase, default 60, configuration), 110 to 175 screens in an Uber Eats-class program. Many users will use the system at once: runs are resumable, single-flight per program, tenant-scoped, concurrency computed from provider limits, fair queue, quotas. Compass output will change a little in future: the readers tolerate unknown keys and flag drift.

B7. WHAT "GOOD" MEANS (the gates test exactly this)
SUFFICIENT: a weak consumer can build a real screen from its task card without asking. FREE: the pack does not bind the front end. FITS: every file and every task is within its budget and big apps work through slices. CORRECT: every node valid, traceable and honest; no invented Locked fact; research rules obeyed. ROBUST: bad inputs, a failing route, a changed model, a crash do not break it. SCALES: cost, time and rate limits behave as modelled. WORTH IT: each content bundle earns its place. For big apps additionally: program-wide coverage, cross-app coherence, task cards inside budget, resume with identical bytes.

B8. WHY EACH MAJOR CHOICE EXISTS
- Freedom enforced by SCHEMA (closed vocabularies, tier ceilings, no layout fields, a form-word lint, a freedom probe): a prompt asking the model to "stay neutral" fails; a schema that cannot hold layout cannot leak it.
- The Spec Graph is canonical and the Pack is its deterministic render: edits, changes and re-packaging for another consumer never rewrite content; the same graph gives the same bytes (cacheable, diffable).
- Byte-stable bodies and an identical prefix bundle: every worker reads the same prefix, so provider caching can work and consistency does not depend on order.
- Budgets as a self-consistent MECHANISM (index 6k, shard 4k, module 3k, slice 5k, front-end allowance 4k, task 28k): a worker must never be handed more than it can use; the packager fails the build rather than truncate.
- Screen counts DERIVED by rules (entities, flows, roles, integrations, a system set, peers): a hard-coded count is wrong for every app; the cap is a per-app capacity, not a target.
- Phase 1 = current release (in), Phase 2 = backlog (later), consent at G1.5: the first release must be a working product (the Thorough export's Dispatch module has 0 core screens and 19 extended ones); a user's own deferral is never relabelled.
- Trust graded per field: Compass's priority and structure are weak, quotes are strong, Research is only a Default when official or corroborated: a wrong Locked fact is the worst error.
- Three voices (MUST, USUALLY, COULD) in separate places, COULD in its own file: workers over-comply with whatever they read; ideas must be offered, never imposed.
- A library-neutral bridge (information shapes, interaction intents, a needs inventory, shared blocks, asset needs, motion intents, tokens as the handshake): the front end looks up components in ANY library or MCP once, without Spec naming one.
- The why layer (personas, stories, journeys with emotion) and the mock data model (a hero skeleton by code, hero content by the model, other modes by code): the preview is how the owner judges the app, and good motion and empty states come from knowing the moment, not only the fields.
- Tokens by code with contrast asserted: a model guesses hex values; code computes accessible palettes.
- Checks as CODE at three gates, every validator as code, repair by a short mechanical ladder: code proves structure better, instantly and the same every time; the independent Verify agent is for deep apps where the risk and the result matter most.
- A portable call contract (one JSON object, local validation, one targeted re-ask, split on truncation, no model or provider in Spec's code): the temporary Haiku-class model will be replaced by Chinese and American providers; nothing may depend on one.
- Free local tools only: no network call in the run path except the gateway; nothing about a user's app goes anywhere else.
- A standalone Bench: Spec must be testable and demonstrable before it is wired into the main flow.

B9. HONEST LIMITS (do not hide these in your report)
Nothing is Proven until its gate passes; every number marked [J] is an estimate; the Haiku-class model's judgment on the Plan is unknown; the writer's real output limit and speed are unrecorded (S0 records them); web facts about tools are mostly secondary sources (smoke-test each); a self-check cannot judge meaning (the owner at G2, the front end's questions, G3, and for deep apps Verify do); visual consistency across parallel workers needs the front end's own pilot step.

C. THE ENGINE, STEP BY STEP (the logic in the order it runs; the appendices hold every detail. Appendix letters: A = doc 18, B = doc 17, C = doc 16, D = doc 15; "D 4.2" means doc 15 section 4.2. Where a step says "code" no model is involved.)

C0. RUN CONTROL
A run is keyed by (program, input hash). One active run per PROGRAM (single-flight; the same input hash joins the running one, a different hash waits or supersedes). Every batch is checkpointed under (program, input hash, step, batch) and the key also carries the call-spec, prompt, schema and library versions and the route fingerprint, so a deployment mid-run never mixes versions. A crash, rate limit, credit stop or budget refusal ends the run PARTIAL; RESUME continues from the last checkpoint and ends with the same bytes as an uninterrupted run. Writes are idempotent; the result cache is tenant-scoped (key: tenant, step, input hash, route fingerprint, prompt version, schema version, library version). The run streams spec.event.v1 events (like Research's resumable SSE): plan, step started/finished, calls, tokens, cost, validators, repairs, banners, gates, partial/resume. Before any model call a ZERO-COST PREVIEW shows the derived profile, inventory count, phases and an estimated cost range; a run whose estimate's upper bound exceeds the remaining budget is refused with a plain message. Spec is the single writer of the graph.

C1. INTAKE (code; D 3, A 1.2)
Read the Compass export through compass-intake (formats 1, 2, trimmed; ignore unknown keys; raise drift flags per format_version; read consumer_views first, then the Brief for tiers and provenance). Read Research through its reader and pack(need_card, token_budget) by Brief id; Research partial/skipped/failed gives a thin lane marked as such. READINESS: fatal ONLY when there is no idea statement or no feature (Spec hands the orchestrator a plain list for Compass; Spec itself asks nobody); everything else proceeds as thin_input with missing roles derived and marked assumed. All upstream text (quotes, Research items) is untrusted DATA (no tools on any call, delimiters, instructions inside data ignored). Compass-origin IDs are carried when the node is the same and aliased on merge or split; Spec-minted IDs live in their own namespace (SCR-S012) so a later Compass SCR-029 cannot collide.

C2. TRUST GRADING (code; D 3.4)
Per field, not per label: a feature's existence is Locked if a verified quote supports it; its priority is Default unless the user ranked it; Compass's structure is Default; a Research item is Default only if official or corroborated (R21 to R23), Open if single_source, unused if unverified; store rules, accessibility floors and the fixed stack are Locked BY POLICY (provenance policy:<id>@<date>, V-33, accepted by V-17) and ONLY rules that are in the dated policy sheet itself; Research platform_constraints are Default at most (a stricter one becomes a Default requirement plus a confirm item); design opinions (one primary action per screen, at most two type families) are Default. A field the sources do not support is null or assumed with provenance (library, policy, research id): NEVER filled to look complete.

C3. PROFILE AND SIZE (code; D 4.1, B 7, A 1)
Profile floor from the tier and size band; raise by content; compact, standard or deep selects: the Product lane shape (one combined call; skeleton plus per module; plus per-app shells and a compliance pass), the Design lane shape (automatic direction; three directions; three plus dark-mode parity, script-fallback checks and per-role variants), cards (at least 3, 5 or 8 acceptance scenarios; 8 includes permission-denied and conflict), Contract v0 depth, content depth by size (doc 17 section 7 table), Verify use (deep on, standard optional, compact off), pack form.

C4. THE PLAN (code, then ONE call SPEC-PLAN on the deep route; D 4, B 2, A 1.2)
CODE derives the screen inventory by R-INV (D 4.2): start from Compass's structure as a proposal (derive from the Brief for format 1); an entity a role can create, edit or manage gets a list (if many), a detail and ONE form screen with a create/edit mode; a view-only entity gets list or detail only where a flow needs it; join/log entities get no screen; every flow step is a screen or a documented state or intent of a screen (a step that only confirms is a state unless it carries its own data); every role has a home unless it has a single destination; screens serving one purpose for several roles are ONE screen whose regions and actions differ by role; every integration needs its setup, consent or permission steps; search and filter are regions and actions of the list screen; peer check from Research screen patterns (add as Default or record why not); dialogs, sheets and toasts are not screens. SYSTEM SET (D 4.3): sign in and up (method variants are states), verify code, forgot/reset, account or role chooser, profile, settings, language, notification settings, notifications inbox, help and contact, legal links, ACCOUNT DELETION (store requirement), consent and age gate when minors/health/identity data, onboarding only when the value needs explaining, permission rationale per sensitive permission; launch, error, maintenance, update-required and offline are states and global behaviours, not screens. SCREEN TYPES are a closed vocabulary (auth, onboarding, list, detail, form, wizard, search, dashboard, calendar, map, chat, media, checkout, confirmation, status, notifications, profile, settings, report, permission, legal), each owning a state set and standard behaviours in the state library, instantiated by code. THE ONE CALL decides merges and splits (merge trivial pairs; split a screen whose slice exceeds the cap) and writes the release proposal, modules, roles and access skeleton, entity owners and personas (compact: the whole product, integrations and the main journey). RELEASE PLANNING (D 4.5, doc 05 section 5): one scope cap per app per phase (default 60, configuration). Phase 1 = features `in`, Phase 2 = features `later` with reason user (never relabelled), capacity or first_release. Procedure: take the features behind Compass's phase core as the Phase 1 candidates; PULL-IN RULE (each role's core journey must run end to end inside Phase 1); add the system set and the minimum operations screens a Phase 1 flow depends on; if an app still exceeds the cap defer the lowest journey-criticality features with their dependents; NEVER defer a user-evidenced must without the user's consent; G1.5 consent is mandatory whenever a capacity deferral is proposed and is the I-4 override record; "everything in one release" is allowed, recorded and warned. A later feature keeps an OUTLINE in the scope ledger and has NO screen nodes (V-19); the whole-scope data model and Contract v0 are written once (later entities and operations flagged later); no in node depends on a later node (V-28). Ordering inside a phase: user-evidenced must first, then journey criticality, dependency depth, peer prevalence, the user's own ranking; never demote a Locked must. At G1.5 the run PAUSES at the Freeze (always for deep); nothing from Screens starts before approval; a changed split re-runs only the affected screens.

C5. THE PRODUCT LANE (calls in parallel after the plan; D 5.8 to 5.12, B 3, B 4, A 1.2)
SPEC-PLAN's skeleton fixes modules, the roles and access matrix, entity owners. PROD-MODULE (one per module, standard route): reads that module's Compass slice and pack(need_card) for its Brief ids; writes entities with typed fields, rules and derived-field formulas, lifecycles (statuses, transitions, role-gated), the CUSTOM operations (domain actions with typed request and response, errors, role gates, idempotency), and user stories with acceptance (each cites an in feature or a policy id; an assumed story is never voice must). A shared entity has ONE owner module and is referenced elsewhere. CODE derives everything derivable: CRUD operations from entities and the access matrix, JSON Schemas, the OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton, pagination, the error taxonomy, the auth matrix. PROD-INTEG (one record per integration need from the plan: provider-neutral flow, interruptions, PENDING TIMEOUTS, webhooks and events, a mock adapter behaviour; interrupted external flow and pending timeouts are REQUIRED for any provider-side flow). PROD-JOURNEYS (about 4 flows per call, against the planned inventory ids): emotion, moments that matter, unhappy paths; first-run and returning and cross-app and recovery variants for deep. Personas come from the plan. Every model-written field needs provenance; a weak model over-fills optional fields: unknown stays null or assumed.

C6. THE DESIGN LANE (one DSGN call; code builds the tokens; D 2, B 5, A 5)
The model writes the direction (mood and personality, audience context, emotional goals per journey stage, motion personality, depth, shape, density, imagery stance, typographic personality, delight budget as a number, dark-mode stance, what to avoid: the generic template), the VOICE LINE, the ambition dial (refined, expressive, immersive: a floor of intent, never a ceiling), the seed colour and closed-set axes, a type personality, and UNBOUND asset needs (brand mark, app icon, splash, empty-state art, clips, audio and haptic cues). Three directions for standard and deep that differ on at least two closed axes (and by at least 60 degrees of seed hue when no brand colour is Locked); one automatic for compact. CODE builds the DTCG tokens per direction (palette ramps and dark scheme by HCT, semantic and state colours, a data-visualisation palette, elevation, motion durations and easings, type scale, per-script fallback families from a dated table of free fonts, spacing, radius) and ASSERTS WCAG 4.5:1 for body text; a user's brand colour stays Locked and the text on it is derived; spring and blur presets stay the front end's ext.* tokens. Policy invariants (accessibility floors, touch targets, contrast) are Locked by policy; design opinions are Default. A dated platform capability sheet gives each capability a tier (A standard, B needs a development build or native module, C not supportable) flagged at G2.

C7. JOIN, GATE 2 AND THE FREEZE (code; A 3.1, D 8)
Gate 2 checks the lanes (roles, lifecycles, contract lint, vocabulary across apps, tokens and contrast, capability tiers, scope ledger, release and inventory, every integration need has a record, every in feature has a story). Failures go to the repair ladder (one re-ask to the owning call). Then the FREEZE: roles, entities, operations, inventory, navigation, tokens, direction, personas, stories, journeys, integrations, the GLOSSARY and the HERO SKELETON become read-only for Screens. A gap Screens finds in a frozen node gets ONE additive re-ask to the owning Product call, then is listed at G2. Code mints the hero skeleton (for every entity as many records as it has lifecycle states or the count of its class, whichever is larger; relations by code; stable ids, the same in every app) and builds the glossary (entity, role and status names, key verbs, Design's voice line; at most 0.7k tokens).

C8. THE SCREENS LANE (after the Freeze; D 5.7, 5.7a, B 1, B 2, A 1.2)
GLOSS-L runs first (one call: the glossary into the source language and every extra language). Then SCRN in parallel batches (screens per call = clamp(floor(0.5 x writer max output / average card tokens), 1, 4), derived from the profile). Each card (never says where or how): purpose; typed route parameters and guards; access; entry points, exits, deep link; information REGIONS (key, what, bind, importance primary|supporting|optional, freshness, SHAPE with attributes, optional use_block, cardinality bucket, live) listed alphabetically with NO order and NO position; inputs (semantic type, validation); list behaviour; ACTIONS (key, importance, INTENT from the closed vocabulary, precondition, effect = at most three typed steps call OP-x / go SCR-y / stay / external_flow name, guard = structured predicates never an expression string, errors, flags optimistic/offline/idempotent); STATES and what each must communicate (library states instantiated by code); copy keys (namespaced by screen id, minted by code) with SOURCE-language text written in the same call; analytics with consent; accessibility specifics; acceptance scenarios (GIVEN, WHEN, THEN); stories; USUALLY (descriptive, with an evidence class, never an instruction); mock references by entity and state; confirm items. COULD entries (Open only, at most 3 per screen, intent and effect, a basis such as a journey moment, signature moments included) go in screens/<id>.could.md. States are never written by the model when the library has them. The freedom lint (V-25) reads free text AND identifiers (keys ending in _button, _cta, _modal, _sheet, _tab, _banner, _toast, _chip or _now name a widget or trigger).

C9. HERO RECORDS, BEHAVIOURS, LOCALES (in parallel with Screens; B 4, A 5)
MOCK-HERO fills the skeleton's content (names, descriptions, quantities, prices, image briefs: subject, count, avoid-list; never URLs, never real brands, marked synthetic); a value that appears in two entities is DERIVED by code from the parent record; related entities go in one call. CODE makes the other mock modes: empty, busy (scroll volume), extreme (only the allow-listed naughty-strings categories plus locale pools), broken (error taxonomy to failure injection per operation), offline (cached data, queued actions), demo accounts per role (a demo code or an example.com email, never a phone number), seeded recipes, behaviours (latency, paging, expiry, realtime scripts, provider callbacks). No ID number and no unmasked phone number is ever generated. BEHAV writes only the app-specific global behaviours (session, offline and sync, error taxonomy and recovery, loading, permissions, notifications, i18n and right-to-left, analytics, client state slices, media fallbacks; the rest is library; the required categories are checked by V-35 including interrupted external flows). COPY-L locale passes (at most about 300 strings per call, streamed behind Screens, flagged needs_native_review; Indic scripts are token-heavy).

C10. ASSEMBLE (code; D 5, 6, A 2)
Commit the graph; render Markdown and YAML from the JSON (the model never writes pack files); shard by topic; project each screen's CLOSURE to the fields it uses (bound fields and lifecycle states, operations and their errors and recovery rows, access rows, rules, source copy, token names, the bodies of the blocks it uses, the route targets of its navigation effects); slice; detect shared BLOCKS (exact bind set plus role-visibility hash, ids minted once with aliases; names by code); build needs.json (bucketed, normalised needs for ONE library lookup and a gap list), assets.json, motion intents, the pilot picks (3 to 5 screens per app covering each shape cluster and screen type on the primary journey with the highest block reuse); build TASK CARDS (reads at most task_read_budget 28k including the front end's 4k allowance), the BUILD PLAN (waves W0 to W7, interface freeze after foundation, disjoint file ownership, capability_class never a model name, parallelism_hint = min(wave size, k_fe) from the consumer profile), the prefix bundle (AGENTS.md, INDEX.md and the build-plan prefix files, stable first, identical for every worker), INDEX.md (hierarchical, no sizes or hashes), MANIFEST.json and index.json (versions, hashes, token sizes, produced_with, checked_by), the content hash (what G2 binds) and the package hash (per consumer profile). Bodies are byte-stable. The packager reports every file and task total and FAILS the build on a breach it cannot re-shard.

C11. GATE 3, VERIFY AND THE REPAIR LADDER (A 3, doc 19 section 3)
Gate 3 = `spec check`: the whole suite V-01 to V-45, the builder-needs rule (BN-01 to BN-17: present, default or assumed; a missing need ends the run partial and never reaches G2) and the coverage matrix. Failures follow the ladder by what the validator reads: model-written node (R-code, then ONE re-ask per node in the whole run, batched per call kind, then R-flag); frozen-node gap (one additive re-ask, then listed); generated file (Spec bug: fail the build loudly). Deep apps then pass through the Verify agent (structure critic at the Freeze, a canary per task card, final critic, patches Spec applies, at most 2 LLM rounds). Nothing is delivered with an unmarked hole.

C12. WHAT THE OWNER SEES (G1.5, G2; D 9.5, A 3)
G1.5: the app map, roles and access, entities in plain words, the inventory and the PHASE SPLIT for the user's yes. G2: summary first; the app map; flows; a CONTENT MAP per screen (what it shows and does, labelled illustrative); data in plain words; what differs from the approved Brief (merged, split, added, phased); assumptions; the confirm list ranked by code (money, legal, identity first, top 20); capability tiers; store rules in plain words; research suggestions with include and exclude toggles; degraded nodes; the list of mechanical code fixes and flags; checked_by (and critic_vendor) ; risks. G2 binds the content hash. A pack with any builder need missing never reaches G2.

C13. AFTER G2: CHANGE AND RE-PACKAGING (D 10.5, doc 05)
Every node records the hash of the inputs it was written from. A token or copy edit (L1) recompiles with no re-plan; adding or changing a feature (L2) re-runs that module's Product call, its cards, contract additions and a check of touched nodes; a re-approved Brief regenerates nodes whose input hash changed; starting Phase 2 is the Scope Change Protocol applied to the backlog (Phase 1's approved baseline stays immutable; Phase 2 gets its own); adding an app (L5) is a new program version; switching the front-end consumer is RE-PACKAGE ONLY (code, zero model cost, same content hash).

C14. OPERATIONS AND SAFETY
Concurrency k = max(1, floor(TPM share / (input tokens per call x calls per minute per worker))), bounded by request and output limits and max_parallel, adapted by additive increase and multiplicative decrease on rate limits; weighted fair queue per tenant; quotas; circuit breaker per route; a credit or rate stop WAITS and RESUMES (never a silent fallback to a weaker route); a per-run report (calls and tokens by step, latency, retries, validator results, repairs, banners, cost against estimate); alerts on estimate drift above 30 percent; packs are content-addressed; evidence/ never goes to the front end; a secret and personal-data scan runs on packs (no keys, no personal data copied into fixtures).

C15. THE DATA LIBRARIES YOU BUILD (data files, not code; dated, with source URLs where they come from the web; omit what you cannot verify)
State library (required states and standard behaviours per screen type with default acceptance scenarios); system screen set with conditions; scenario library; Module Library v1 (about 12 modules: auth, profile and settings, notifications, list-detail-edit, search and filter, order or booking lifecycle, checkout and payments, location, chat, reviews, admin tables, onboarding); the dated store-policy sheet (read the OFFICIAL Apple and Google pages; every rule with source URL and date); the platform capability sheet with tiers; the delight-pattern library; vocabularies (17 information shapes with attributes, about 38 interaction intents with destructive and irreversible flags, input semantic types, motion intents, asset kinds, mock profiles, screen types, state kinds); the exact-synonym table; the error catalogue (structured agent-readable errors {code, severity, where, why, fix}); the script-fallback font table; name and place pools (Kannada curated; Marathi, Hindi and English via Faker locales); the naughty-strings category allow-list; consumer profiles (weak-default = the temporary Haiku-class route, standard-default, large-context-default, values from each provider's CURRENT documentation, dated, with source_url; never from memory); the Stack Kit (fixed data; if unpinned say so in the manifest).

0. FIRST
- Take your commit checkpoint (D-154): commit what is pending, tag pre/spec-agent-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>, cut a new branch from the tip that has the gateway's Claude provider and the Research overhaul (today feat/llm-providers). This is a NEW agent, not an overhaul of an existing one, so no owner yes is needed beyond this prompt. Branches and tags may be pushed (D-155). Nothing merges into main without the owner's yes.
- Read: CLAUDE.md, GLOBAL_RULES.md, docs/implementation/CURRENT_STATE.md, DECISIONS.md (D-125 to the end, especially D-159, D-162, D-166, D-171, D-172), docs/research-agent/spec-contract.md and compass-contract.md, ADR 0014 (call-spec layout), .importlinter, the nine inputs in docs/compass/research-inputs/ (README first), and this prompt first, then Appendices A to D (docs 18, 17, 16 and 15) in full.
- Live runs use the temporary Haiku-class route through the gateway's Claude provider (MODEL_ROUTES; never name a model in Spec code). Your preflight must say whether the key for the route's vendor is present, without ever reading or printing .env or a key. If it is absent, finish every offline phase and report; do not stop work.

1. WHAT SPEC IS FOR (so you can decide the cases this prompt did not foresee)
Pipeline: Compass (approved Brief) -> Research -> SPEC -> G2 (the owner approves) -> the front-end engine (NO agent between Spec and the front end for small and medium; for DEEP apps the thin Verify agent checks between Spec and G2 and IS built now, doc 19 section 3), an LLM that writes the Expo / React Native / TypeScript app (iOS and Android), then backend and QA. Spec reads Compass and Research and writes ONE Spec Pack: a folder with a global reference file (INDEX.md), global files, one small card per screen, a contract, tokens, copy, a build plan. Its only purpose is to give the front-end engine what it needs to build, so the front end does not have to think about the product and can spend its effort on how each screen looks and feels.
The line that decides every field: MEANING is Spec's (who, what, data, rules, flows, states, words, API contract); EXPRESSION is the front end's (layout, components, motion, imagery). Spec never writes a layout, a widget name, a position, a pixel, a colour outside the tokens, or a per-screen visual hint. It gives tokens and a design direction as a starting system the front end may extend (ext.* tokens are the front end's). Over-specified input makes the front end build the same template for every app; under-specified input makes it guess.
The weakest configured consumer is the design target: today a Haiku-class model, later any other. So cards are explicit and flat, and every budget is a configuration value derived from a consumer profile, never a constant.

2. THE DESIGN IN TWENTY LINES (doc 15 has the detail; these are the non-negotiables; items 14, 15 and 18 are REPLACED by the text here and in sections 2B to 2E, and doc 19 then doc 18 win wherever they differ)
1. One agent, three lanes (Product, Design, Screens) plus a deterministic assemble step; Product and Design in parallel, join, Freeze, Screens in parallel batches, assemble. Single writer of the Spec Graph.
2. The Spec Graph stays canonical (typed nodes, edges, Locked/Default/Open tiers, provenance, stable IDs, tombstones, aliases). The Pack is its deterministic render: same graph and same consumer profile give the same bytes.
3. Freedom is enforced by SCHEMA: closed vocabularies (importance primary|supporting|optional, screen_type, state_kind, action flags, bind targets, token names), short typed free text, a tier ceiling per field (doc 15 2.3), no layout fields, no hints in the front-end pack. V-24 (blocker) and V-25 (form-vocabulary lint on free text AND identifiers, a WARNING in v1, tuned on the corpus; keys ending in _button, _cta, _modal, _sheet, _tab, _banner, _toast, _chip or _now name a widget or trigger). An action's effect is a list of at most three typed steps (call OP-x, go SCR-y, stay, external_flow name); a guard is a list of structured predicates, never an expression string; every action has an importance (primary or secondary).
4. Information regions have an importance level and NO order and NO position; they are listed alphabetically by key. Actions are intents with precondition, effect, errors and flags (optimistic, offline, idempotent); the trigger (button, swipe) is never stated. States say what must be communicated, never how it looks. Region and action keys are stable and become testIDs.
5. Pack layers are named in words: index, global, module, screen (never "tiers" or "lanes"). Budgets are a MECHANISM with starting defaults that must be SELF-CONSISTENT (the configuration loader REFUSES an inconsistent set): index at most 6k tokens, a global shard at most 4k with at most 6k of shards per task, a module file at most 3k, a screen card 1 to 2.5k (hard 3k), a screen file (card plus its generated closure = the slice) at most 5k, the front end's allowance 4k, task_read_budget 28k (the caps sum to it, so a one-screen task always fits), whole_pack_tokens derived as task_read_budget minus the allowance minus the task card (about 22k). The packager shards by topic, projects closure to the fields a screen uses, splits heavy screens, counts with the consumer profile's tokenizer (or a conservative factor of characters over 3 until measured), and FAILS the build on a breach after trying to re-shard.
6. File bodies are byte-stable: no version, hash, token size, dependents or timestamp inside a body (they live in MANIFEST.json and index.json, which tools read and the model does not); keys sorted, LF endings, locale-independent ordering. INDEX.md is hierarchical (global files, apps, modules; each module file lists its screens) and holds no size or hash. G2 binds the CONTENT hash (graph plus content files, independent of the consumer); the package hash (bytes for one consumer profile) is recorded beside it, so re-packaging never voids an approval. prefix.bundle.md (AGENTS.md, INDEX.md and the files named in build-plan prefix_files, stable first) is identical for every worker.
7. Screen count is DERIVED by rules (doc 15 4.2 R-INV), never fixed; the user's tier sets a detail profile floor (compact, standard, deep) that content can only raise. A system set (doc 15 4.3) is added when accounts exist.
8. One scope cap per app, configuration, default 60 (a starting value, not a limit the owner set). Phase 1 is the current release (status in) and Phase 2 the backlog (status later), exactly as doc 05 section 5 defines them. A deferral sets the feature later with a reason: user (never relabelled), capacity, or first_release (beyond Compass's approved core set). Procedure: start from the features behind Compass's phase core; apply the pull-in rule (each role's core journey must run end to end inside Phase 1; the real Thorough export has 0 core and 19 extended screens in its Dispatch module); add the system set; defer the lowest-criticality features only if an app is over the cap; never defer a user-evidenced must without the user's consent. G1.5 consent is mandatory whenever a capacity deferral is proposed and IS the I-4 override record. A later feature keeps an OUTLINE in the Scope Ledger and has NO screen nodes (V-19). Whole-scope data model and Contract v0 once (entities and operations of later features flagged later). Starting Phase 2 is the Scope Change Protocol applied to the backlog as one batch. No in node depends on a later node (V-28). At G1.5 the run PAUSES at Freeze; nothing from Screens starts before approval.
9. Inputs through shared readers: packages/compass-intake (extract Research's intake/formats.py so a Compass change is fixed once; if risky, copy it and keep contract tests on both) and a Research reader plus pack(need_card) (agents may not import each other; extract to a shared package or reimplement with the same contract tests; decide and log it). Tolerate format 1, format 2, trimmed; ignore unknown keys; raise drift flags; a readiness pre-check is fatal ONLY when there is no idea statement or no feature (Spec hands the orchestrator a plain list for Compass; Spec itself asks nobody); everything else proceeds as thin_input, with missing roles derived and marked assumed.
10. Trust is graded PER FIELD (doc 15 3.4): feature existence Locked if a verified quote supports it; priority Default unless the user ranked it; Compass structure Default; Research Default only if official or corroborated, Open if single_source, unused if unverified (R21 to R28); store rules, accessibility floors and the fixed stack are Locked BY POLICY (provenance policy:<id>@<date>, V-33, accepted by V-17), and ONLY rules that are in the policy sheet itself; Research platform_constraints are Default at most (a stricter one becomes a Default requirement plus a confirm item); design opinions (one primary action per screen, at most two type families) are Default.
11. IDs: Compass-origin IDs carried when the node is the same, aliased on merge or split; Spec-minted IDs in their own namespace (SCR-S012).
12. Spec's own reads are budgeted: a skeleton call over a SUMMARY of the Compass view, then one Product call per module reading that module's Compass slice plus pack(need_card, token_budget) for its Brief ids; a shared entity has one owner module. Every call input is assembled by code and capped at min(0.5 x effective context of the route, route limit); an overflow SPLITS the step, never truncates. FUSION RULE (doc 18 1.2): two jobs share one call only if the estimated output is at most half of the profile's max_output_tokens, the input stays under the cap, AND the fused schema compiles within the profile's limits (max_nullable_fields is a PROFILE value, 16 today); otherwise split back into the doc 15 and doc 17 calls. If the first-try NODE pass rate of a call kind is below 85 percent on the proof corpus, the profile un-fuses that kind.
13. Developer readiness: builder needs BN-01 to BN-14 (doc 12) plus BN-15 platform and store rules, BN-16 global behaviour, BN-17 phases and cap. Standard states per screen_type, the system set, standard scenarios and a dated store-policy sheet are DATA instantiated by code.
14. CHECKING (doc 18 section 3 and doc 19 section 3). EVERY size: Spec checks itself in code at THREE GATES: gate 1 after every call (schema and closed vocabularies, ids and edges, bindings and actions, mandatory states, keys, provenance and grounding V-17, V-33, V-36, V-45, shapes and COULD rules, fixtures), gate 2 at the join (roles, lifecycles, contract, vocabulary, tokens and contrast, capability tiers, release and inventory, every integration need has a record, every in feature has a story), gate 3 = `spec check` on the finished pack: the WHOLE suite V-01 to V-45 (V-18 is superseded by V-26), the builder-needs rule (every BN is present, default or assumed; a missing need ends the run partial and never reaches G2) and the coverage matrix. DEEP apps additionally pass through the Verify agent (agents/verify, doc 19 section 3: structure critic at the Freeze, a canary per task card, final critic, repair classes A, B, C, structured patches that SPEC applies, at most 2 LLM rounds, an honest critic_vendor flag); compact never; standard by configuration (verify.profiles, default [deep]). Verify only checks: it never writes into the graph or the pack. evidence/self-check.json and evidence/verify.json are written; MANIFEST.json says checked_by: self_check, or self_check and verify. The consumer probe and the planted-defect test are also PROOF tools under evals/. V-45 GROUNDING, NARROW ON PURPOSE: in a Locked node or a research-derived Default (1) every numeral with its unit occurs in the cited quote or item (normalise digits, separators and Indic numerals; number words, lakh and crore scaling and derived arithmetic are NOT checked and are listed as unchecked for G2); (2) provider and brand names come from CLOSED lists (the dossier list and the Brief's own tokens); (3) typed rules with the same subject and the same condition but different values are flagged. V-45 runs FLAG-ONLY until PS-7 shows at most 5 percent false positives; then its downgrade of the node to Open assumed is switched on (a configuration of the checker); flags are shown at G2.
15. Shared packages (AD-33: agents import shared packages only): packages/spec-core (graph, validators V-01 to V-45, renderer, packager, slicer, build planner, loaders, and the `spec check` command anyone can run) imported by agents/spec (agents/verify, built for deep, imports spec-core and the gateway only). The legacy packages/spec-builder and packages/spec-loader are REFERENCE and tests to learn from, not dependencies. The layering edit in .importlinter is lead-only: make it with a D- entry.
16. Resumable: every batch is checkpointed under (program, input hash, step, batch); a crash, a rate limit or a credit stop ends the run PARTIAL and RESUMES (Research could not, D-167). Idempotent writes; a single-flight lock per PROGRAM (one active run per program, doc 02); a tenant-scoped result cache; the checkpoint key carries the call-spec, prompt, schema and library versions.
17. Concurrency is COMPUTED from the consumer profile (tokens-per-minute share over per-call tokens times calls per minute), adapted by additive increase and multiplicative decrease on rate-limit responses; weighted fair queue per tenant; never a silent quality drop.
18. REPAIR LADDER (doc 18 section 3.2). R-code, ONLY these mechanical fixes, each LOGGED and counted on the G2 page: sort and normalise bytes; mint a MISSING id (a duplicate id is never fixed by code); instantiate a missing standard state, behaviour, scenario or system screen from the library (provenance library, tier Default); an exact-synonym map for closed vocabularies (else R-ask); drop an unknown optional field; downgrade a Locked claim without evidence to Default; plus the packager's re-shard. R-ask: ONE targeted re-ask of only the failed items (the item, the validator message word for word, the schema fragment, the allowed values), at most one per NODE in the whole run, BATCHED per call kind. R-flag: library default, Compass's own value or drop the optional item, mark assumed or degraded, list on G2; never an unmarked hole. A binding the role may not see: R-ask, else drop it and list it at G2; a missing copy key: R-ask, else mark the region copy_unspecified and list it. An invented fact is removed, never repaired into a Locked one. By what the failing validator reads: a model-written node goes down the ladder (also at gate 3: one re-ask of its owning batch if not re-asked yet); a gap in a frozen node gets one ADDITIVE re-ask to the owning Product call, then is listed at G2; a GENERATED file (closure, budgets, bytes, routes, needs, blocks) that fails is a Spec bug and FAILS THE BUILD. Every step has a default EXCEPT the Plan: a Plan call still invalid after its re-ask ends the run partial and resumable (a fallback route first, if configured). NO quality stop: only a weak_route banner when more than 15 percent of NODES needed a re-ask for one step; the money budget is the only spend control. Every LLM call has a versioned call spec, a mock handler and a deterministic fallback (rule in CLAUDE.md).
19. All upstream text (Brief quotes, Research items) is untrusted DATA: no tools on any Spec call, delimiters, schema-validated output, instructions found in data ignored.
20. No guessing: a field the sources do not support is null or marked assumed with its provenance (library, policy, research id), never filled to look complete.

2B. THE FINAL ARCHITECTURE (doc 18; it overrides everything above and below wherever they differ; read doc 18 in full)
- PIPELINE AND CALLS for compact and standard: intake (code) -> SPEC-PLAN (deep; compact: also writes the product, the integrations and the main journey; standard: plan, skeleton, personas) -> in parallel PROD-MODULE (one per module: entities, rules, lifecycles, custom operations, stories), PROD-INTEG (integrations and events: provider-neutral flow, interruptions, pending timeouts, webhooks), PROD-JOURNEYS, DSGN (three directions for standard and deep, one automatic for compact; no signature moments) -> join and gate 2 -> FREEZE (also freezes personas, stories, journeys, integrations, the GLOSSARY and the HERO SKELETON) -> GLOSS-L FIRST (one call putting the glossary, at most 0.7k tokens, into the SOURCE language and every extra language; if it fails after its re-ask the Brief's own terms are used and the locale calls are marked degraded) -> in parallel SCRN (cards, SOURCE copy and COULD entries with signature moments in one call; copy keys namespaced by screen id, minted by code), MOCK-HERO (fills the skeleton, never mints ids), BEHAV (the app-specific global behaviours), COPY-L locale batches streamed behind (at most about 300 strings per call) -> assemble and gate 3 (`spec check`), with G2-SUMMARY (fast; tables from code, one paragraph from the model, a template if it fails) in parallel. Typical call counts [J]: compact about 14, standard about 38 when the writer can output 32k tokens or more per call; about 25 and 70 at 8k. RECORD the writer's real max_output_tokens, output speed and max_nullable_fields in the profile in S0, recompute doc 18's estimate table from them and report it.
- CODE DOES MORE. TOKENS by code: the model picks closed-set axes, a type personality and (if the user gave no brand colour) a seed colour; code builds palette ramps and the dark scheme (HCT), semantic and state colours, a data-visualisation palette, elevation, motion durations and easings, the type scale and per-script fallback families from a dated data table of free fonts; it computes the real contrast of every text-on-surface pair and asserts WCAG 4.5:1 for body text; a brand colour the user gave stays Locked and the text on it is derived; three directions differ on at least two closed axes (and by at least 60 degrees of seed hue when no brand colour is Locked). MOCK MODES by code: empty, busy, extreme, broken, offline, demo accounts per role, seeded recipes. HERO SKELETON minted by code at the Freeze: for every entity as many records as it has lifecycle states or the count of its class, whichever is larger (12 to 20 for a primary entity and up to 30 in deep, 3 to 5 for the others, compact 8 to 12), relations assigned by code, stable ids, the same in every app; a value that appears in two entities (an amount, a person's name) is DERIVED by code from the parent record, never written twice, and related entities go in the same MOCK-HERO call; cards cite hero records by entity and state and the packager resolves them; V-41 checks that every lifecycle state has a record; the hero calls fill the skeleton's content. ASSETS: data-bound needs by code from media fields and hero briefs; UNBOUND needs (brand mark, app icon, splash, empty-state art, clips, audio and haptic cues) written by DSGN; block detection is exact and block names are made by code. The GLOSSARY (entity, role and status names, key verbs, Design's voice line; at most 0.7k tokens) leads the prefix of every SCRN and COPY-L call. Only token NAMES go into the shared prefix (values stay in tokens.dtcg.json); signature moments are COULD entries written by SCRN, and code collects the entries of the primary journeys into a DELIGHT BLOCK of at most 0.4k tokens in the prefix.
- MOCK PROFILES SHIPPED: compact empty, typical, broken, offline; standard plus busy; deep all six (extreme on request below deep). SWITCHES B1 to B5 of doc 18 section 5 (fused calls, source copy inside SCRN, busy and extreme by code, bound asset needs by code, block names by code) are CONFIGURATION with their default shown; PS-10 has the owner compare code-made and model-written lists on 5 previews.
- THE STATIC PACK (doc 18 2.2): G-1 a graph version is immutable and the same graph renders the same bytes; G-2 every screen file holds its card and a closure that INCLUDES the bodies of the blocks it uses and the route targets of its navigation effects (route name, typed parameters, guard), a task bundle dedupes block bodies at read time (a typical slice is then about 3.3 to 3.8k and a task carries TWO TO THREE slices; an over-cap slice caused by a card's size is a class (a) repair: the packager moves bulky detail to screens/<id>.detail.md, then ONE re-ask shortens the card, and only a budget that cannot be met after both is a Spec bug); G-3 one identical prefix (index, global rules, direction and motion intents, token names, the delight block, the glossary); G-4 no build-order words (wizard steps, journey stages and GIVEN-WHEN-THEN are product content); G-5 one owner per shared thing, copy keys namespaced by screen id by code; G-6 every id used to build resolves inside the slice or the prefix (informational ids are marked info); G-7 honest tiers; G-8 self-describing. `spec check` verifies each. The one-file form (APP_SPEC.md) only for a consumer that reads about 80k or more. AGENTS.md says plainly that visual consistency across parallel workers needs the front end's pilot step.
- THE LLM CALL CONTRACT (doc 18 4): one JSON object per call; the gateway picks the strictest structured-output mode; the prompt carries the schema in short text, the glossary and the closing line "Return ONE JSON object that matches the schema, no other text" (the word JSON must appear); TOLERANT PARSE: strip reasoning blocks and code fences, take the first JSON object that parses and fits the top-level shape, salvage the finished items of a truncated array; validate locally; on truncation redo only the unfinished items in smaller batches (a fused call, the Plan included, splits back into its parts); static-first prompt layout (rules, vocabularies, schema, examples; then frozen facts and glossary; then the slice); RESULT-CACHE KEY (tenant, step, input hash, ROUTE FINGERPRINT, prompt version, schema version, library version), where the fingerprint is an opaque hash the gateway computes from what the route resolves to (Spec never sees names); PS-9 bypasses the cache (a harness argument, not a runtime flag). A Gate 3 re-ask wave (when one is needed) re-assembles, re-runs spec check and re-translates changed copy keys; V-37 error cases left after their one re-ask become a blocked entry on the G2 page (waive with a recorded mobile_fit_waiver or send the screen back for a split).
- FREE TOOLS (doc 18 6 and notes/spec-external-tools-research-2026-11-14.md): ONLY free, open-source or free-tier tools; NO network call in Spec's run path except the gateway; pin versions, record licences (python-stdnum and pycountry are LGPL), one smoke test per tool in S0. Use now: Faker (en_IN, hi_IN and mr_IN exist; there is NO Kannada: a curated pool; never its ssn or bank providers or random phone numbers; a script check fails a fixture whose people or places fell back to English), Big List of Naughty Strings (MIT, pinned commit; ONLY the categories Reserved Strings, Numeric Strings, Special Characters, Unicode Symbols, Quotation Marks, Two-Byte Characters, Emoji, Right-To-Left Strings, Zalgo Text, Scunthorpe Problem; a test fails if the pinned file's headings change), Babel (test that format_decimal(1234567.891, locale="en_IN") gives Indian grouping), phonenumbers (validation and formats only: phone numbers appear in mock data ONLY MASKED, and demo accounts sign in by a demo code or an email at the reserved example.com domain), python-stdnum (a fixture FAILS if any ID-like value passes validate(); ID numbers appear only masked; a deny-list also fails a digit run of 9 or more, a plate-like value or an unmasked name@bank id, since stdnum has no validator for plates, UPI ids or account numbers), script fallback fonts (Noto families, SIL Open Font Licence; NOT researched: verify the licence and script coverage of each family in S0 and record source and date), coloraide (assert the WCAG ratio; APCA is not confirmed), jsonschema, Pydantic, openapi-spec-validator (the run path is Python-only), a tolerant JSON parser. Proof only: promptfoo (needs Node 22 or newer) and free LLM tiers in a SEPARATE proof route map (no runtime flag) with the four synthetic inputs only until the owner confirms the nine exports hold no personal data. Translation services are outside the policy. Front-end tools (Expo MCP, component-library MCPs, Unsplash, Lottie, Maestro, MSW, Reanimated, Style Dictionary) are NOT Spec's.

2C. RESULT FIRST (doc 19 section 1; it overrides doc 18 where doc 18 traded result for cost or speed)

Doc 18 traded some result for cost and latency because the owner had asked for lean small and medium apps. The owner now says result comes first and big apps matter most. So:

| Doc 18 said | Now |
|---|---|
| No Verify agent now; reserved for deep, **not built** | **The Verify agent is built now, for deep apps** (§3). Compact: off. Standard: configurable (`verify.profiles`, default `["deep"]`), because small and medium keep their no-latency path |
| Un-fuse a call kind below 85% first-try node pass | **Below 90%**; for deep no fusion beyond the split forms of docs 15 and 17 unless the proof shows 90% or better for that kind |
| B3: `busy` and `extreme` made by code from 12 to 20 hero records | The **model writes every record that appears in a list or first-view screen** (deep: up to 30 per primary entity); code only multiplies for scroll volume and builds `empty`, `extreme`, `broken`, `offline`; the owner A/B of PS-10 stays |
| Three directions for standard, one for compact | **Three for standard and deep**, one for compact |
| Cost estimates drive design | Cost is a **hard cap only** (§5). Where quality and cost or speed conflict, quality wins; a deep run may take 12 to 30 minutes |
| Canary out of the delivery path | Out for compact and standard; **in the delivery path for deep** (a canary per task card) |
| OI-40: big apps without an independent check | **Resolved**: deep apps get the Verify agent |

Everything else in doc 18 stands (three code gates and every validator as code for all sizes; the repair ladder; the portable call contract; free local tools; the static pack).

2D. BIG APPS (doc 19 section 2; the owner says the big one is MORE important)

**2.1 What a big app is.** The user's tier is Thorough, or content raises the profile to `deep` (doc 15 §4.1: two or more apps, sensitive data, three or more integrations, three or more locales or a right-to-left script, offline-first use, four or more apps or eight or more modules). Typical: a **program** of two to six apps (customer, courier or driver, vendor, one or more admin portals), **50 to 60 screens per app** at the front end's per-run capacity (`scope_cap_per_app_phase`, default 60, configuration), so **110 to 175 screens in a program**; 11 or more modules; 20 or more entities with 8 to 15 fields; 10 to 20 integrations; three or more locales; 10 to 20 roles; web portals next to phone apps.

**2.2 What deep adds** (doc 17 §7, made concrete): the Product lane = skeleton, one call per module, per-app shells and a **compliance pass** (data protection, retention, consent, from Research's platform and trust views); the Design lane = three directions, dark-mode parity and script-fallback checks, **per-role variants** (consumer against admin); cards with at least 8 scenarios including permission-denied and conflict; Contract v0 with idempotency, concurrency, webhooks and versioning notes; 100 or more stories including admin and operations; journeys including first-run, returning, cross-app and recovery; blocks with depth variants and cross-app blocks; needs and asset needs with sourcing and licence rules; motion intents per role; all six mock profiles, realtime scripts, cross-app coherence, locale packs, extreme-data performance checks; all behaviour categories plus localisation depth and performance targets per screen class; an analytics plan with a measure per role; a store-listing kit; a QA test-data matrix; COULD up to 30 per app, each with a basis.

**2.3 Program structure.**
- **One Spec run per program**; one G1, one G1.5 and one G2 per program; the scope cap and the Phase 1 / Phase 2 partition are **per app** (doc 15 §4.5).
- **Shared modules** (account, notifications, payments, help, legal) are specified **once** and referenced by every app that needs them; a shared screen keeps one id and is counted once per app that includes it; role differences are regions and actions by role, not copies.
- **One data model and one contract for the program** (one OpenAPI with per-app tags); an entity has one owner module and the same fields in every app (V-11 checks vocabulary across apps).
- **Cross-app coherence of mock data:** the hero skeleton gives one order one id and one timeline in the customer, courier, restaurant and admin apps; the hero calls for related entities run together (doc 18 §5).
- **Packs:** `global/` and `contract/` shared; `apps/<APP>/` per app with its modules and screens; the build plan has a **program-level interface freeze** (shared types, token names, store-slice shapes, route maps per app) and per-app waves.

**2.4 Scale mechanics.** A program pack is 500k tokens and up and is **never read whole** by anyone. Task cards (at most `task_read_budget`, 28k including the front end's allowance) are the only way in; waves W0 to W7 as in doc 15 §5.13: foundation, shared, **pilot slice (W2, 3 to 5 screens per app, one task each)**, canary fan-out, polish; an interface freeze after the foundation wave; disjoint file ownership; `parallelism_hint = min(wave size, k_fe)` from the front-end consumer's own profile; heavy cards move bulky detail to `screens/<id>.detail.md`; the packager splits an over-budget task and fails the build only on a breach it cannot re-shard.

**2.5 Spec's own run mechanics for big programs.** About 100 calls per 60-screen app without Verify (about 130 with it), a program of four apps about 2.3 times that; checkpoints per batch (program, input hash, step, batch, versions, route fingerprint); resume with identical bytes; a single-flight lock per program; concurrency computed from the profile and adapted on rate limits (doc 15 §10.3); a rate-limit storm ends the wave `partial` and resumes; progress events stream the whole time; estimates and time are measured, not promised (a run of 12 to 30 minutes is normal).

**2.6 Big-app quality rules** (extra to the validators):
1. **Program-wide coverage:** every role, entity and flow has a screen in some app; a role with no home screen is an error.
2. **Cross-app coherence:** same entity, same fields and statuses everywhere; the same hero ids; the same copy terms (the glossary spans apps).
3. **Role-variant screens:** one id, regions and actions by role; a screen split by role only when the purposes differ (doc 15 §4.2 rule 4).
4. **Web portals** (admin, vendor back office) are exempt from the column limit of V-37 and keep the rest.
5. **G1.5 is a hard gate** for deep: the phase split with the pull-in rule is shown and consent recorded (the Thorough export's Dispatch module has 0 core and 19 extended screens and must still land in Phase 1).
6. **Phase 2** features keep outlines in the ledger with no screen nodes; starting Phase 2 regenerates incrementally.
7. **Verify** (§3) runs; a deep pack never says `checked_by: self_check` alone.

**2.7 Fixtures for big** (the builder's generator, doc 16 §6): the real Thorough export; a synthetic **Uber Eats-class program** of four apps (about 140 screens: customer about 52, courier about 23, restaurant about 28, admin portal about 40); a synthetic single app of 60 screens with entities of 8 to 15 fields and checkout-class screens binding five operations; an ERP with hundreds of entities; twenty integrations; 90 core screens; global-only providers; a partial research store; five locales including a right-to-left one.

**2.8 Acceptance for big (PS-12):** (a) on the 60-screen synthetic app and on the real Thorough export, every task card is within `task_read_budget` with no unrepaired breach, every validator is green or flagged with a reason the owner can read, and the prefix bundle is identical across tasks; (b) Thorough: dispatch is in Phase 1, zero Locked nodes without evidence, canary blocking questions at most 0.3 per screen on average [J]; (c) a run killed at wave k resumes and ends with the same bytes as an uninterrupted one; (d) the cross-app coherence tests pass on the Uber Eats-class program; (e) Verify finds at least 90% of the 22 structural planted defects (80% per kind) and its meaning-defect catch is reported against the self-check's; (f) measured cost and time are within 1.5 times the estimate recomputed from the recorded profile.

2E. THE VERIFY AGENT FOR DEEP (doc 19 section 3; build it)

**3.1 Boundary.** `agents/verify` (import name `mde_verify_agent`) imports `packages/spec-core` and the gateway only; Spec and Verify import each other never (AD-33). They meet through a **`VerifyPort`** defined in `spec-core`; the composition root of the standalone app injects the Verify implementation. A profile without Verify skips the port.

**3.2 What it does (it only checks; it never writes into the graph or the pack):**
1. **Structure critic at the Freeze** (`standard` route; a different vendor if configured, else `critic_vendor: same` is stated): the Brief against the frozen structure: contradictions, missing flows, unreachable or dead-end screens, role and entity mismatches, cross-app disagreements, a Locked fact dropped or changed.
2. **Validators per batch** (the same code as the self-check; Verify re-runs them, it does not own different ones).
3. **A canary per task card** (the weakest configured consumer profile; it reads exactly the task card's reads and returns `{outline[], blocking_questions[], assumptions[], acceptance_coverage[{criterion, satisfiable, how}]}`; not code). Deep: **every card**. Standard with Verify on: every card; compact: never.
4. **Final critic** with the coverage matrix and the freedom checks: spec against Brief, contradictions across apps, the confirm list's ranking, what differs from the Brief.
5. **G2 summary** (the plain-language paragraph and tables, as in doc 18).

**3.3 Repair.** Each defect carries a class: **A** code fix (Spec applies, at most 3 passes, must converge), **B** lane call (Spec re-writes the node; counts as a round), **C** needs decision (routed to Product; counts inside the limit). Verify returns **structured patches** `{node, field, change, reason}`; **Spec applies them** (single writer); touched nodes are re-verified by hash. **At most 2 LLM rounds across the Freeze and the final pass**; then the node is `degraded` and listed at G2. A node already re-asked under doc 18's ladder may take one Verify-driven repair if it has not used its Verify round.

**3.4 Independence, honestly.** Only one vendor may be configured: Verify still runs and the pack says `critic_vendor: same`. **A bigger or dearer route is not assumed to be a better critic** (Research measured the opposite, D-172): the critic's route is chosen by the PS-7 measurement. The canary uses the weakest consumer profile.

**3.5 Outputs.** `evidence/verify.json` (findings, patches, rounds, the canary results per task card), `MANIFEST.json` `checked_by: ["self_check", "verify"]` and `critic_vendor`, the G2 data (what was checked, what was repaired, what is still open). Config: `verify.profiles`, `verify.canary_share`, `verify.max_llm_rounds` (2).

A config file (spec-config.yaml) holding EVERY number in doc 15 marked [J]; a consumer-profiles data file (doc 15 11.4) with entries weak-default (the temporary Haiku-class route), standard-default and large-context-default: fill the values from each provider's CURRENT documentation, dated, with source_url; never from memory; where you cannot verify, leave the field unset and say so. Fields include nominal and EFFECTIVE context, max output, tokenizer (counter or factor), caching mode, structured-output mode and schema limits (max optional or nullable fields, depth, enum size), per-minute limits, max parallel, prices, long-prompt surcharge (threshold and multiplier; Haiku 5.5 is five times above 100K prompt tokens per D-171: keep every call below it), source_url, checked_on.

S1 DETERMINISTIC CORE (no model, no money)
- Libraries v1 as DATA: the state library (required states and standard behaviours for each screen_type in doc 15 4.4, with default acceptance scenarios), the system screen set (doc 15 4.3 with conditions), the dated store-policy sheet (read the OFFICIAL Apple and Google pages; every rule with source URL and date; a rule you cannot verify is omitted and listed, never included), the scenario library (doc 15 7.2).

Portable schemas (section 6).

NO component variants and NO per-screen-type composition rules (doc 15 16.1); system-wide invariants only.

Quick three times, then Standard three times; report RANGES (a single run decides nothing).
