4C. THE SPEC BENCH (doc 19 section 4; the owner asked for a mock static front end for testing; build it)

**4.1 What it is.** A separate app, **not part of the main flow**, built like the Research app: one process, one address (**`http://127.0.0.1:8130/`**), its own static front end (`apps/spec-bench/`, plain HTML, JavaScript modules and CSS, no build step, like `apps/research-console/`), its own backend (`agents/spec`'s `api` package, FastAPI), file-based storage under `agents/spec/.runtime/`, `scripts/spec_app.py start|stop|status|logs|restart`, `just spec-dev`, `spec-app-*`, `spec-test`. **It imports nothing from `mde_flow`, `context-api`, `web` or any other agent**, uses no database, and has its own composition root. Future integration into the main flow is a thin adapter over the documented contract (`docs/api/spec-agent.md`: input = a Compass export plus a Research output; output = a Spec Pack folder, its manifest and the events); **do not build that adapter now**.

**4.2 It plays the owner's journey and the front end's role.** The left rail is the journey: **1 Inputs → 2 Preview (zero cost) → 3 G1.5 → 4 Run → 5 G2 → 6 Hand-off to the mock front end.** Everything the owner needs is in plain words; budget and spend are always visible.

**4.3 Auto-select of inputs** (a pure function with tests; the UI and the CLI use the same one):
- **Discover** Compass exports (`docs/compass/research-inputs/*.json`, `agents/spec/.runtime/inputs/`, and any directory in `SPEC_INPUT_DIRS`), classify each with `compass-intake` (format version, tier, size band, derived profile, readiness, drift flags) and discover **Research outputs** (`agents/research/.runtime/runs/*/run.json` and `research.json`, status complete, partial or failed).
- **Match** a Research run to a Compass export by the recorded input hash (and, if absent, by the Brief id and content hash); prefer the newest complete run; show gaps ("no Research run: Spec runs with a thin research lane and says so").
- **Auto-select** proposes: the smallest export of each class (Quick yoga: compact; Standard produce marketplace: standard; Thorough freight: deep), the synthetic Uber Eats-class program, and the best Research run for each, with the reason for every choice and a one-click override. A run can also start with Compass only.
- **Headless:** `uv run python -m mde_spec_agent bench auto --size deep` and `bench run --input <path> [--research <path>] [--offline]` use the same function, so the builder (Claude Code) can drive end-to-end tests without clicking.

**4.4 The mock front end** (the front end's role, **static, never a design**):
- **Consumption simulator:** three modes against a chosen consumer profile: *all at once* (only if the pack fits that profile's `whole_pack_tokens`; otherwise it says why not), *one by one* (pick a screen: the exact files and bytes a worker would read, prefix plus card plus closure, and the token total against the budget), *parallel* (the task cards grouped by wave, worker slots from the profile's `k`, a dry-run timeline).
- **Consumer probe runner:** the weakest profile (Haiku) reads a task card and returns the outline, blocking questions and assumptions (live, inside the budget; an offline stub otherwise).
- **Screen content map:** for each screen a static page of what it must communicate and do (regions grouped by importance with no position, actions with intent and effect, states, source-language copy, hero records on the chosen mock profile); MUST, USUALLY and COULD are visibly different voices; **labelled "illustrative: the final layout is the front end's"**.
- **Journey walkthrough:** choose a role and a journey (stories, emotion line, moments that matter, unhappy paths) and step through the screens by their declared entries and exits; switch the mock profile (`empty`, `typical`, `busy`, `extreme`, `broken`, `offline`).
- **Navigation graph:** an SVG of apps, roles and routes with role filter, `in` and `later` styling, unreachable screens and dead ends highlighted.
- **Data and contract:** entities and lifecycles, operations (from OpenAPI), fixtures, mock behaviours, integrations with their interrupted-flow and pending-timeout rules.
- **Pack explorer:** the tree with token sizes per file and per task; the budget report; every validator result; the builder-needs matrix; the coverage matrix; the self-check report (code fixes, re-asks, flags, banners); the Verify report (deep); the G1.5 and G2 views; a diff between two pack versions by hash; run history; the budget page.
- **Static export:** one self-contained `preview.html` per pack (works offline, no network) so a pack can be handed to anyone.

**4.5 Safety.** A pack holds user text and model text: render everything with `textContent` or a sanitizer, never `innerHTML`; allow-list link schemes (copy the pattern of `apps/research-console/lib/safe.js`); the bench never executes anything from a pack.

**4.6 Tests.** Offline: the helper and static tests like `apps/research-console/tests`; a **test-only fake app** with scripted doubles (like `agents/research/tests/e2e/fake_app.py`, port 8150) for browser checks; the auto-select tests against the nine exports; the e2e journey test through the API (inputs → preview → run offline → G1.5 → G2 → simulator). Live: one smoke run inside the budget. **The composition root cannot select a test double** (a test checks it, as for Research).

PS-11 AND PS-12 AND THE EXTENDED GATES (doc 19 section 7)

- **PS-11, the Bench:** auto-select proposes the right pairs on the nine exports (snapshot tests); the offline e2e journey passes through the API and in a browser against the fake app; the consumption simulator reproduces the packager's task totals; the preview renders every screen of the Standard and Thorough packs without script injection (a poisoned quote test); a live smoke run stays inside the budget; the app starts, stops and restarts with `scripts/spec_app.py`; the composition root cannot select a double.
- **PS-12, big apps:** §2.8.
- **PS-7 is extended:** the self-check's planted-defect test (22 structural plus 8 meaning) and **Verify-for-deep's** catch rates, reported separately, with the critic's `critic_vendor` stated.
- **PS-9** runs the 200 cases; **PS-10** adds the owner's comparison of code-made and model-written lists and assets on 5 previews.

4B. THE CONTENT MODEL (doc 17; the owner asked for it on 2026-11-14; it ADDS to the phases above, read doc 17 in full)
- Three voices and the rule of silence: MUST, USUALLY, COULD; anything not said is the front end's to decide. COULD is Open only, intent and effect only, each with a basis (a journey moment, a research item, the capability sheet, a library pattern), at most 3 per screen (caps by profile), in its OWN FILE per screen (screens/<id>.could.md, read by the polish pass, not part of the build slice), an assumed basis stays assumed, outside the G2 hash, and the form-word lint is a warning (V-42).
- A bridge to ANY component library and tool without naming one. Every region has a shape (the 17 shapes with attributes of doc 17 2.2; other:<name> goes to the gap list) and optional use_block, cardinality bucket, live; actions carry an intent from the closed vocabulary (doc 17 2.3); inputs keep the doc 15 5.7a semantic types plus code, secret, quantity, toggle. The vocabularies are versioned DATA files. AFTER the Screens lane, code builds needs.json (bucketed and normalised needs with anatomy, gestures, motion and accessibility role, for ONE library lookup and a gap list), blocks (EXACT bind set plus role-visibility hash, never fuzzy; ids minted once with aliases; near-duplicates are block_candidate warnings; each screen file's closure carries the bodies of the blocks it uses (doc 18 G-2) and a task bundle dedupes them at read time), assets.json (data-bound needs by code, unbound ones written by DSGN; subject, count, avoid-list; no lighting, placement or crop; app icon, adaptive icon and splash as brand_mark needs) and motion-intents. Tokens are the handshake with any library (role names, state roles, durations and easings; spring and blur stay ext.*; the tokens are the Default starting theme the front end themes its library with). Never name a library, component, tool, package or version.
- The why layer: personas, user stories with acceptance (every in feature has one, every screen cites one; V-40), journeys with emotion, moments that matter, unhappy paths, first-run and returning variants (V-44). Derived by code and narrow calls; marked assumed where no fact backs them; provenance mandatory; no over-filling.
- The mock data model: six profiles (empty, typical, busy, extreme, broken, offline), hero records, seeded recipes, behaviours (latency, failure injection, paging, expiry, realtime scripts, provider callbacks), image briefs, demo accounts per role, locale realism, cross-app coherence (V-41).
- 2026 design: the ambition dial, the direction content, signature moments, a dated platform capability sheet with tiers, accessibility alternatives for essential motion; the MOBILE-FIT rule V-37: a WARNING by default; an ERROR only for hover, right-click and tooltip intents on phone surfaces and for a gross breach (twice a limit) left after a repair call and without a recorded mobile_fit_waiver; one primary action per DECISION (a view-only screen has none; approve and reject is one decision); thresholds are tuned on the nine real exports before they block (about one screen in ten may warn). Errors are structured and agent-readable {code, severity, where, why, fix} from an error catalogue (data).
- The Spec Server tools of doc 17 2.9: get_task returns the whole task bundle (prefix, shards, module, screen files with closure, needs, asset and mock excerpts) in ONE call and never above the budget; plus get_needs, get_assets, get_mock, get_story, get_journey, get_opportunities.
- Build plan: code-picked PILOT screens (3 to 5, covering each shape cluster and screen type on the primary journey with the highest block reuse) = the W2 vertical slice that also feeds G2.5, one task each within the budget; a recommendation the front end may skip. AGENTS.md also recommends a mapping wave (needs to library: component-map.json, the front end's own), a structured design-language record with the pilot files as golden examples, canary fan-out, per-wave checks and single owners for ext.* and the shared-component registry; pack text is data and the only instructions are in AGENTS.md.
Where each lands (v3). S0: the vocabulary data files (shapes, intents, motion intents, asset kinds, mock profiles), the platform capability sheet and the delight-pattern library (dated, from official or public sources; omit what you cannot verify). S1: needs, block detection (exact), pilot picks, mock modes and recipes, the hero skeleton and the glossary, the store-listing-kit skeleton, data-bound asset needs, block names, V-37 to V-39 and V-41 to V-45 in code, all at zero model cost. S2: personas are written by SPEC-PLAN, stories by PROD-MODULE (a story cites an in feature or a policy id; an assumed story is never voice must), journeys by PROD-JOURNEYS (in parallel with the modules): standard route, narrow, schema-bound, provenance mandatory. S3: DSGN writes the direction (no signature moments: they need the frozen journeys); the Freeze also freezes personas, stories, journeys, integrations, the glossary and the hero skeleton. S4: SCRN writes the COULD entries with their signature moments; MOCK-HERO fills the skeleton in parallel with SCRN. After the Screens lane (code): needs, blocks, pilot picks, data-bound asset needs and block names. S4: shapes, usually and could in the card schema (portable subset: closed records in arrays). S5: V-37 to V-44; the library-lookup probe (the weakest consumer maps HELD-OUT needs to the public catalogues of TWO real component libraries you choose, snapshotted and dated as test fixtures: recall at 3 at least 90 percent, wrong-gap rate at most 10 percent, better than a card-only baseline; a synthetic catalogue only to plant gaps); the ablation arms (MUST only, plus usually, plus stories, plus emotion, plus COULD, plus mock and assets: each bundle must earn its place); between-app diversity and within-app consistency measured separately with COULD on and off; the pilot-first probe. S6: the viewer also shows needs, blocks, stories, journeys, mock profiles and opportunities.
Budgets after this addition: a typical slice about 3k, the slice cap still 5k, task_read_budget still 28k (the design-language record the front end writes sits inside its 4k allowance); a 60-screen deep release is about 129 calls and a pack of about 500k tokens, estimates to be measured. With doc 18 a slice also carries its block bodies and route targets (about 0.3 to 0.8k more; the cap stays 5k and V-26 checks it), and a 60-screen deep release is about 100 calls without Verify.

5. THE EDGE-CASE SUITE
One test per ID of doc 15 section 12 (SPC-IN, SPC-RS, SPC-SC, SPC-MD, SPC-FE, SPC-CH, SPC-OP, SPC-UX: 113 cases in doc 15, plus SPC-CL, SPC-MK, SPC-ST, SPC-DG, SPC-SZ: 35 cases in doc 17 SPC-FN: 36 cases in doc 18 section 7 and SPC-BG: 16 cases in doc 19 section 6, so 200; the prefix avoids clashes with doc 05 and doc 13 IDs). Your fixture folder mirrors the IDs (spc-in-01, spc-rs-07, spc-md-06 ...). A link check FAILS the build when an ID in doc 15 has no fixture or a fixture has no ID. Fixture kinds: real, mut (mutations of the nine inputs), syn (your generator), mock (gateway behaviours: invalid JSON, truncation, refusal, a 429 storm, "no credits", a slow route, a process killed at batch 7, concurrent starts), cfg (profile and route variants). Most are offline.

The SPC-BG cases (doc 19 section 6):

| ID | Situation | What Spec does |
|---|---|---|
| BG-01 | Four apps share account, notification and help screens | specified once, one id, counted once per app that includes them; role differences by region and action |
| BG-02 | One screen serves several roles | one id; regions and actions by role; role-visibility part of the block match |
| BG-03 | One order appears in four apps | one hero id and timeline from the skeleton; related entities written together; V-41 checks coherence |
| BG-04 | An app derives more screens than the cap and holds user-evidenced `must` features | defer by criticality with reason `capacity`; never a `must` without recorded G1.5 consent; conflict options shown |
| BG-05 | An admin web portal with wide tables | exempt from the column limit of V-37, other mobile-fit rules kept; marked `surface: web` |
| BG-06 | Hundreds of entities | shards by entity cluster; an owner module per entity; the data model never exceeds a shard cap; task cards name only the clusters they need |
| BG-07 | Twenty integrations | one `PROD-INTEG` batch per five integrations; each with flow, interruptions, pending timeouts, events; a Gate 2 record check |
| BG-08 | Five locales including right-to-left | glossary into all; locale batches by 300 strings; RTL as a global behaviour; script-fallback tokens; `needs_native_review` |
| BG-09 | A rate-limit storm in wave 3 | the wave ends `partial`; concurrency halves; resume from the checkpoint; identical bytes |
| BG-10 | The critic finds two apps disagreeing on an entity's statuses | class B patch to the owning module; Spec applies; touched nodes re-verified |
| BG-11 | A task card would exceed the read budget | the packager splits at a module boundary; a heavy card moves detail to `.detail.md`; never truncated |
| BG-12 | The process is killed at wave 4 | resume from the last batch checkpoint; same bytes as an uninterrupted run |
| BG-13 | Phase 2 starts after approval | incremental regeneration; Phase 1's approved baseline stays immutable; Phase 2 gets its own |
| BG-14 | A feature changes after G2 (L2) | the change controller files a change set; Spec regenerates the affected slices and tasks; Verify re-checks touched nodes |
| BG-15 | Two canary runs of one task card disagree | both recorded; the blocking questions are the union; the card is judged by the stricter result |
| BG-16 | The budget cap is reached mid-run | the call is refused, the step checkpoints, the run ends `partial` with a plain message; the pack is never delivered half-checked |

6. THE CALL CATALOGUE, ROUTES AND SCHEMAS
- Routes: Spec's calls name routes fast, standard, deep (doc 15 11.2); the gateway maps them. Plan: deep; modules, integrations, journeys, design, hero records, behaviours: standard; screens: fast or standard; glossary translation, locale passes and the G2 summary: fast; no critic in the delivery path for compact and standard; for deep the Verify calls are in it (structure critic and final critic: standard route, a different vendor if one is configured; the canary: the weakest configured consumer profile). All routes may map to ONE Haiku-class model today; the design must hold when they do.
- Schemas are a PORTABLE SUBSET: flat closed records in ARRAYS, never open maps (ADR 0014), few optional or nullable fields per call (max_nullable_fields is a PROFILE value, 16 today after Claude refused a schema with more than 16 nullable parameters, D-172; the fusion rule consults it), small enums, shallow nesting. The model writes JSON; code renders the Markdown and YAML of the pack. The gateway sanitises the dialect; you add an offline schema-compile check for every call schema against every configured profile's limits, in PS-0.
- NO OVER-FILLING: a weak model fills optional structured fields the source does not state (Haiku at low effort, D-172). Every call spec says: leave unknown fields null or assumed; every filled field needs provenance (user, library, policy, research id); validators check provenance and bindings. Effort is configured per model in the gateway (effort_floor); you never put effort or a vendor in a call spec.
- Each call spec: versioned, schema, mock handler, deterministic fallback, input budget check, a checkpoint key. Few-shot examples come from the libraries.

7. MODEL AND PROVIDER INDEPENDENCE (rule 14, owner instruction, repeated because it is the owner's)
No model or vendor name in Spec code, prompts, schemas, packs or tests (except dated profile data). Vendor, model, price, effort, schema dialect, token accounting and error mapping live only in the gateway and its config. The Anthropic provider sends NO cache markers today (D-171): assume no caching until a profile enables it; the estimate takes cache_share from the profile. Prices are read from the profile and pricing.yaml, never hard-coded. Switching the FRONT-END consumer re-packages (code, no model call, same content hash); switching Spec's own route changes nothing in Spec. Two routes need not give identical specs; both must pass the same validators and probes (outputs are validated, not compared).

8. MONEY: THE HARD CAP (doc 19 section 5; the owner: max USD 5, no exceeding, stop in any way possible)

- **Money is integer micro-USD.** The Spec spend record lives at `agents/spec/.runtime/spend-record.json` with a cross-process lock (copy the mechanism of `agents/research/src/mde_research_agent/spend/`); the cap `SPEC_LIVE_BUDGET_USD` defaults to **5.00** (set in the launch environment, never in `.env`), tripwire `SPEC_TRIPWIRE_USD` **4.50**; restartable only by the owner.
- **Reserve before every live call:** worst-case cost = input tokens times the input price plus the call's maximum output tokens times the output price (plus the long-prompt surcharge, from the profile). If `spent + reserved + in-flight > cap`, the call is **refused**, the step checkpoints and the run ends `partial`. After the call, reconcile with actual usage.
- **Tripwire:** at 4.50 no new wave starts; in-flight calls finish; the run checkpoints; only report-writing (no model) continues.
- **No bypass:** every Spec and Verify model call goes through one wrapper that enforces the reserve (a test uses a scripted gateway that tries to overspend and must fail to). The environment's global `LLM_BUDGET_USD` must also be at least the cap and never lower than the spend record's.
- **Several ways to stop:** the reserve check, the tripwire, `POST /api/stop` (graceful: checkpoint and end `partial`), SIGTERM, and `scripts/spec_spend_check.py` (an independent sum of the ledger and the spend record that exits non-zero above the cap).
- **A run whose estimate's upper bound exceeds the remaining budget is refused with a plain message** before it starts. This is the **money budget, the only spend control** (no quality stop, no second flag).
- **Order and allocations (starting values, USD):** price check 0.05; PS-3 0.35; PS-4 0.20; PS-5 0.50; PS-6 0.30; PS-7 0.25 (with the meaning set, the critic arm and Verify-for-deep catch rates); **PS-12a** a synthetic 60-screen app with Verify 0.60; **PS-12b** the real Thorough export with Verify 0.60; PS-8 extras 0.15; PS-9 live 0.20; PS-10 0.30; Bench live smoke 0.05; reserve 0.45; **PS-12c** the Uber Eats-class program with Verify about 1.0 **only if at least that much remains**. **Never drop** the Thorough and 60-screen runs; drop in this order when short: PS-12c, PS-9 live runs, PS-10 extra arms, PS-5 repeats (keep two). The price check recomputes every figure; stop if reality is more than three times the estimate.

9. DO NOT
- Do not put layout, widgets, positions, per-screen hints or colours outside tokens into any pack field or any prompt.
- Do not call the web from Spec. Do not write app code or pseudo-code. Do not choose libraries (the Stack Kit is fixed data; if it is unpinned, say so in the manifest).
- Do not modify Compass or Research except to extract the shared readers (D- entry, tests green on both sides). Do not build the front-end engine, the backend, or the adapter that would plug Spec into the main flow (design it in docs/api/spec-agent.md only). The Bench imports nothing from mde_flow, context-api, web or any other agent.
- Do not add a runtime flag, a readiness check or a quality-triggered stop (the money budget is the only spend control). Do not call any network service from Spec except through the gateway. Do not generate ID numbers or random phone numbers, do not use Faker's ssn or bank providers, do not use naughty-strings categories outside the allow-list.
- Do not hard-code a number from doc 15 in logic: it is configuration. Do not tune code or prompts to make a gate number pass; report ranges and say when a number is a single run.
- Do not read or print .env or any key. Do not commit uv.lock from a worktree. Do not merge into main. Do not exceed USD 5.00 by any path.

10. STANDING RULES (carry these; they are the owner's)
Live is one switch, LLM_MODE=live; never propose a second key, flag, check or hook. The builder asks the owner nothing: decide and record in DECISIONS.md. Models only through the gateway, no agent frameworks, no agent loops; web content untrusted. Content in data files; money as integers (micro-USD) never floats; agents import shared packages only; Spec imports no other agent. Conventional Commits with Task: and Refs: footers; commit checkpoints (D-154); branches and tags may be pushed (D-155). Quality beats cost; nothing is Proven until its gate passes. External tools, APIs and data: free, open-source or free-tier only, and only where they help Spec (owner, 2026-11-14). Plain words for the owner: say what is verified and what is not; do not tune code to make a number pass; report ranges.

11. REPORT (when you stop, and at the end of each phase; saved at docs/spec-agent/REPORT-<date>.md)
In plain words, for a non-engineer: what is built and what is not; each gate PS-0 to PS-12 with its numbers (ranges for anything model-written) against the thresholds of docs 16 and 19; per call kind the first-try node pass rate, the repair rate, the R-code change counts and the weak_route banners; the writer profile's recorded limits and doc 18's estimate table recomputed from them; for the big runs (PS-12a, b, c) the program and per-app screen counts, pack size in tokens, task cards and their read totals, calls, minutes, cost against estimate, Verify's findings, patches and canary results, and what the owner should check; the Bench (address, how to start and stop it, what each page shows, how Claude Code can drive it headlessly); the budget booked against the USD 5.00 cap and the spend check result; what surprised you; every decision you made that the docs did not cover (D- numbers); every place you think a document is wrong, with evidence; what the owner should read first (the Thorough G1.5 view, five screen cards, ten probe outputs, the Bench's G2 view of the Thorough pack); the next step. Say honestly when a number is a single run and when a claim is not verified.
